claims: Theology is the systematic study of God, divine beings, and religious truth.
Theology is derived from Greek words meaning "discourse on God".
Biblical Theology analyzes themes of redemption, salvation, and specific narratives across the Old and New Testaments.
Systematic Theology organizes religious doctrines into coherent systems, focusing on themes like God's nature, salvation, and sin.
Historical Theology examines the development of doctrine and theological thought throughout church history.
Practical Theology focuses on applying theology in everyday life, worship, and ministry.
Other forms of theology include Liberation Theology, Moral Theology, and Natural Theology.
Theology is deeply rooted in examining the Bible and its historical development.
Theology involves investigating biblical content, such as comparing the writing styles of the Gospels.
Theology applies biblical truth to contemporary issues, using both faith and critical reflection.
Seminaries and universities offer in-depth programs focusing on historical and systematic study.
